item.title: Xi attends state dinner held by Trump
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
Xi attends state dinner held by Trump WASHINGTON -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Thursday evening attended a state dinner held by US President Donald Trump and his wife, Melania Trump, at the White House. Xi and Peng were warmly greeted by the US presidential couple upon their arrival. The two presidential couples posed for photos and met with guests attending the dinner. Xi and Trump delivered remarks respectively after the dinner began. Xi extended sincere greetings and best wishes for the Mid-Autumn Festival to Americans from all sectors of society who care about and support the further growth of China-US relations. Xi noted that Trump paid a successful visit to China in May, and that the two heads of state exchanged state visits within six months, making history in bilateral engagement. He said common understanding on many issues have been reached during his visit this time, adding new substance to the constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, and providing fresh strategic guidance for bilateral ties. Xi stressed that over 200 years ago, soon after its independence, the United States turned its eyes to China. The two countries started trading with each other, exchanging goods to meet each other's needs and drawing on their complementary strengths. Noting that more than 80 years ago, the Chinese and American people stood shoulder to shoulder in the fight against Japanese militarist aggressors, Xi said such a friendship forged in blood and fire will surely live on through the generations. Over 50 years ago, Ping-Pong Diplomacy between the two countries reopened the door to bilateral exchanges that had been closed for years, Xi said. The older generation of Chinese and US statesmen, with the political wisdom of "a small ball moving the globe," set in motion the historic process of normalizing China-US relations. Xi said the story of an American named Ronald Sakolsky, who more than 20 years ago gave financial support to Chinese desert control worker Yin Yuzhen for her tree-planting effort, touches the hearts of many Chinese people and stands as a shining example of the friendly exchanges between the two peoples. Xi noted that bilateral exchanges have helped promote heart-to-heart communication between the two peoples and cemented public support for China-US friendship and cooperation. Today, China-US relations have come to another historical juncture, Xi said. Trump's pledge to make America great again and China's commitment to achieving great national rejuvenation are both ambitious goals that can surely be mutually reinforcing, he said. He said China and the United States must act as responsible major countries, meet the expectations of the two peoples, keep pace with the trend of the times, and explore a new approach for major countries to get along with each other. Like a river that never stops flowing, history never stands still, Xi said, adding that the friendship between the two peoples is a worthy cause that holds great promise. The two sides should join hands and move forward side by side, nurture the beautiful flowers of China-US friendship, and write a new chapter in their friendly relations, he added. The state dinner was held in a warm and cordial atmosphere, featuring wonderful performances put on by American artists.

item.title: Manila plays dangerous game at Ren'ai Reef
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
Manila plays dangerous game at Ren'ai Reef It is worth noting that the Philippines has a neighbor that has never sought to bully it with superior strength, settle disputes by force, exploit its moments of vulnerability, isolate it through hostile blocs or close the door on dialogue. Yet these are precisely the "sins" that the government of Ferdinand Marcos Jr routinely accuses China of committing. The contrast between such rhetoric and reality is becoming harder for regional countries to miss. Manila has reportedly sought China's help in addressing an oil shortage triggered by the Middle East crisis. It has also welcomed Chinese supplies of chemical fertilizers when the Ukraine crisis disrupted global supplies. But it cannot indefinitely demand economic cooperation while treating every Chinese act of goodwill as an invitation to provoke further confrontation. On Thursday, the Philippines reneged on its commitments and ignored China's warnings by sending a supply vessel to deliver provisions to a warship it illegally grounded at Ren'ai Reef in 1999. The China Coast Guard responded with lawful measures, including on-site monitoring and verbal warnings, according to its spokesperson, who urged Manila to stop provoking trouble, saying the China Coast Guard will continue to conduct law-enforcement and rights-protection activities in the Nansha Islands and adjacent waters in accordance with the law. Manila's now familiar response is to portray China's professional law enforcement as "aggression", apparently on the assumption that being the smaller country automatically confers the status of "victim". But a country's size does not turn an unlawful act into a lawful one, nor does a loud complaint establish who is responsible for a confrontation. The signs suggest that the Philippines is preparing further resupply missions. Should it press ahead with them, China will have little choice but to take necessary measures to stop these unlawful provocations and safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights. The Philippines' schemes violate the spirit of the Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea, which calls on all parties to exercise self-restraint and avoid actions that complicate disputes. They do nothing to advance a peaceful settlement. Instead, they invite miscalculation in waters where regional stability should be a common priority. So the pertinent question is why the Marcos government seems so determined to keep the South China Sea simmering. Domestic political pressures, including public discontent over inflation, may offer part of the explanation. So may the influence of external powers that have little incentive to see regional tensions subside. Certain politicians in Manila appear more interested in serving their own political calculations and the strategic agendas of foreign patrons than in protecting the Philippines' national interests. The question is not who can make the loudest accusations, but who is actually working to prevent a local dispute from becoming a regional crisis. The Philippines would do well to recognize the strategic patience China has demonstrated. Beijing has repeatedly kept channels of communication open, even as Manila has pursued increasingly confrontational tactics. It has not sought to organize a regional coalition to isolate the Philippines, nor has it abandoned dialogue in favor of force. Such restraint should not be mistaken for weakness, still less for an unlimited license to test China's patience. The small-boat theatrics orchestrated by Manila's political "bad apples" should end before they inflict lasting damage on regional peace and the Philippines' own interests. A neighbor that keeps the door to dialogue open is not one to be needlessly pushed toward confrontation.

item.title: Documentary filmmaker shares stories of kindness
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
Documentary filmmaker shares stories of kindness Share - WeChat
During World War II, a 7-year-old Chinese boy gave his birthday egg to an injured American airman after the Doolittle Raid. In return, the airman gave him a penny — a coin the boy kept into old age. In Wuhan, American documentary filmmaker George Retelas, whose grandfather served in the US Navy during the war, shared this story. Such simple acts of kindness, he said, are things we can all do for one another. After several visits to China, he said the real gift he had received was "the people I met".

item.title: Insights offered to push for steady ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
Insights offered to push for steady ties: China Daily editorial Like his address on his arrival at the White House on Thursday morning, President Xi Jinping's speech at the state dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump on Thursday evening was rich in substance and offered important insights into the steady development of China-US relations. Taken together they reveal the principles, perspectives and wisdom embedded in China's approach to Sino-US ties. In his speech upon arrival at the White House, Xi called for strengthened communication, exchanges and cooperation across various sectors, emphasizing peaceful coexistence. In his state dinner address, Xi recalled historic moments in China-US interactions spanning more than two centuries, saying that a friendship forged in blood and fire will surely live on through the generations. This legacy of friendship reflects not only the foresight of statesmen of the two countries and the shared aspirations of the two peoples for a better life, but also the two sides' commitment to peace and justice. This, in part, explains why US people's views of China have warmed since 2022, according to a recent Pew Research Center survey. The improvement underscores the value of China's efforts to foster a more objective and rational understanding of China among US people. The bedrock of the Sino-US relationship has always been the people. By upholding a commitment to people-to-people exchanges, the two sides can strengthen communication and cooperation and fortify trust. The invitation Xi sent to 100,000 young Americans to visit China for study and exchanges over the next five years embodies precisely this long-term vision. By encouraging mutual understanding among younger generations, China is looking beyond the immediate differences to the future. The remarks of Xi are therefore an expression of the sense of responsibility expected of a reliable partner and a manifestation of the recognition of both sides that the "giant ship" of China-US relations needs steady hands on the helm to weather the storms and sail steadily toward a brighter horizon. Time will demonstrate that China is a reliable partner that embraces competition with an open mind and seeks to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation. China's approach reflects its long-term vision and confidence in the future of Sino-US relations. It creates the space and time needed for both sides to manage differences constructively. On his part, Trump said in his meeting with Xi that US-China relations will surely be handled well under the leadership of the two heads of state. Xi's visit will help translate the vision for a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability into actions, providing fresh strategic guidance for steering bilateral ties toward stability.

item.title: Chinese, US first ladies visit National Museum of Asian Art
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-25
Chinese, US first ladies visit National Museum of Asian Art WASHINGTON -- Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Melania Trump, wife of US President Donald Trump, visited the National Museum of Asian Art in Washington on Thursday. Peng and Melania visited exhibition halls including the Peacock Room. Peng expressed appreciation for the US side's return of Chinese cultural relics to China on multiple occasions in recent years, expressing hope that China and the United States would continue to strengthen cooperation on cultural exchanges and cultural heritage protection, and deepen the friendship between the two peoples. After the tour, Peng and Melania watched American teenagers sing Chinese songs together and had cordial exchanges with them. Peng encouraged them to continue studying the Chinese language and culture and to become envoys of friendship between China and the United States. The National Museum of Asian Art is a renowned US institution dedicated to the collection, research and exhibition of Asian art.
